info.title: Workfront Fusion API
info.description:
REST APIs for managing and monitoring your Workfront Fusion resources. Use these APIs to programmatically access activity logs and other Fusion components coming soon.

**Base URL:** https://fusion.adobe.io

**Getting Started:**

 For detailed setup instructions, make sure to visit the [Getting Started guide](https://developer-stage.adobe.com/workfront-fusion-apis/getting-started/).
1. Set up authentication in Adobe Developer Console, as documented [here](https://developer-stage.adobe.com/workfront-fusion-apis/getting-started/authentication/).
2. Obtain required headers (Authorization, x-api-key, x-organization-id, x-gw-region). More details [here](https://developer-stage.adobe.com/workfront-fusion-apis/getting-started/api_headers/).
3. Update permissions for the technical account, as documented [here](https://developer-stage.adobe.com/workfront-fusion-apis/getting-started/technical_accounts/).
4. Make your first API call.

tags.name: Connections
tags.description: Endpoints for managing connections within your organization. These endpoints allow you to list all connections, retrieve details for a specific connection, and view scenarios associated with a given connection.

tags.name: Keys
tags.description: Endpoints for managing encryption keys within your organization. These endpoints allow you to list, create, update, and delete keys used for securing your data and connections.

tags.name: Hooks
tags.description: Endpoints for managing hooks within your organization. These endpoints allow you to list all hooks scoped to a team and retrieve full details and configuration for a specific hook.

tags.name: Data Stores
tags.description: Endpoints for managing data stores within your organization. These endpoints allow you to list all data stores scoped to a team, and retrieve details for a specific data store including its metadata and usage metrics such as record count and storage size.

tags.name: Logs
tags.description: Endpoints for retrieving execution logs within your organization. These endpoints allow you to list all executions scoped to a scenario or incomplete execution.

tags.name: Data Structures

get.description:
Returns a paginated, filterable list of scenarios in the organization.

Supply `teamId` in the property query to restrict results to one team.

**Recycle bin:** pass `property=deleted==true` to list soft-deleted (binned) scenarios instead of active ones. When this filter is present, results are further gated by the `resource_restore` permission — users only see deleted scenarios they're allowed to restore. Without the `deleted` filter, only active scenarios are returned.

post.description:
Creates a copy of the scenario in the target team, applying dependency replacements from the body.
The response body contains the new scenario ID; the `Location` header points to the new resource.

**Rules**
- **Same team**: existing connections may be reused; you can omit replacements for them.
- **Different team**: connections cannot be reused; provide replacements for each required connection.
- If the source scenario uses a **hook**, provide an unused hook in the replacements.
- For **data stores, data structures, and keys**: if you supply IDs in the request, those are used; otherwise they are duplicated in the target team.

parameters.name: scenarioId
parameters.description: Source scenario ID to clone

201.description: New scenario created; response body contains its ID. `Location` header is set to the new scenario URL.

get.description:
Retrieves operation counts for an organization, optionally filtered by team, scenario, and/or package, with optional grouping by dimension.

**Grouping:** Use the `groupby` parameter to break down operation counts by `team`, `scenario`, `package`, or `module`. When set, each time-period entry in the response includes a nested array broken down by the chosen group.

**Date Range:** The `from` and `to` parameters define the time window. The maximum allowed range is 1 year. Results are automatically grouped by `day` or `month` depending on the range.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description:
Start date in ISO 8601 format (UTC). Defines the beginning of the date range for operation counts.

**Note:** Date range between `from` and `to` cannot exceed 1 year.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description:
End date in ISO 8601 format (UTC). Defines the end of the date range for operation counts.

**Note:** Date range between `from` and `to` cannot exceed 1 year.

parameters.name: teamId
parameters.description: Filter results to a specific team. When provided, only operations for this team are returned.

parameters.name: scenarioId
parameters.description:
Filter results to a specific scenario.

**Note:** Requires `teamId` to also be specified.

parameters.name: package
parameters.description:
Filter results to a specific package name.

**Note:** Requires `scenarioId` to also be specified.

parameters.name: groupby
parameters.description:
Group operation counts by a specific dimension. When set, each time-period entry in the response includes a nested array broken down by the chosen group.

**Available Groups:**
- `module` - Group by module name
- `package` - Group by package name
- `scenario` - Group by scenario ID
- `team` - Group by team ID

parameters.name: orderby
parameters.description:
Sort results by timestamp. Prefix with `+` for ascending or `-` for descending.

**Values:**
- `+timestamp` - Oldest first (ascending)
- `-timestamp` - Newest first (descending)

**Default:** Oldest first (`+timestamp`).

parameters.name: property
parameters.description:
Filter results by operations count. When `groupby` is used, filters the nested arrays by their operations value.

**Format:** `operations<operator><value>`

**Operators:**
- `==` equals
- `!=` not equals
- `>` greater than
- `>=` greater than or equal to
- `<` less than
- `<=` less than or equal to

errors: teamId must be a number conforming to the specified constraints

get.description:
Retrieves a summary of total operation counts for an organization, broken down by scenario and team. Use this endpoint to get a high-level overview of operation consumption without time-series data.

**Date Range:** The `from` and `to` parameters define the time window for aggregation. The maximum allowed range is 1 year.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description:
Start date in ISO 8601 format (UTC). Defines the beginning of the date range for the summary.

**Note:** Date range between `from` and `to` cannot exceed 1 year.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description:
End date in ISO 8601 format (UTC). Defines the end of the date range for the summary.

**Note:** Date range between `from` and `to` cannot exceed 1 year.

parameters.name: teamId
parameters.description: Filter results to a specific team. When provided, only scenarios belonging to this team are included in the summary.

parameters.name: scenarioId
parameters.description: Filter results to a specific scenario. Returns the operation count for this single scenario.

parameters.name: package
parameters.description: Filter results to a specific package name.

parameters.name: orderby
parameters.description:
Sort summary results by field. Prefix with `+` for ascending or `-` for descending.

**Sortable Fields:**
- `scenarioId` - Sort by scenario ID
- `teamId` - Sort by team ID
- `operations` - Sort by operation count

**Default:** `-operations` (highest operation count first).

parameters.name: property
parameters.description:
Filter scenarios by their total operations count within the specified date range.

**Format:** `operations<operator><value>`

**Operators:**
- `==` equals
- `!=` not equals
- `>` greater than
- `>=` greater than or equal to
- `<` less than
- `<=` less than or equal to

delete.description: Deletes queued webhook events for the specified hook. Provide a specific set of ids via repeated params (`?id=a&id=b`, max 50), or `?all=true` to clear the queue (optionally excluding `?excludeId=a&excludeId=b`). Returns the ids that were deleted plus any that could not be (with a reason); if any id fails, the response status is 409 while the deletable rows are still removed.

parameters.name: hookId
parameters.description: Numeric ID of the hook whose queue to delete from.

parameters.name: all
parameters.description: Delete all queued webhook events for the hook.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the queued webhook event to delete. Repeat for multiple (`?id=a&id=b`). Maximum 50.

parameters.name: excludeId
parameters.description: ID of the queued webhook event to exclude when deleting `all`. Repeat for multiple (`?excludeId=a&excludeId=b`). Maximum 50.

200.description: All requested events were deleted. `deleted` lists them; `failed` is empty.

409.description: At least one event could not be deleted, so the request is flagged as failed (deletable rows are still removed). `deleted` and `failed` report the per-id outcome.

id.description: Unique scenario identifier within the organization context.

description.description: Optional longer description shown in the UI.

folderId.description: Folder ID for organizing scenarios; omit if the scenario is not in a folder.

usedPackages.description: Identifiers of app packages or modules referenced by the scenario (for example integrations).

isInvalid.description: True when the scenario is considered invalid (for example disabled after repeated errors).

isActive.description: Whether the scenario is linked and eligible to run.

isLocked.description: True while the scenario cannot be executed (for example still being configured).

isPaused.description: True when execution is paused after errors until the scenario is resumed.

sequential.description: Whether modules in the scenario run strictly in order (sequential execution).

lastEdit.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the last modification to the scenario.

scheduling.description: Schedule definition when the scenario is triggered on a timer (shape depends on scheduler settings).

hookId.description: Webhook device ID if the scenario is driven by an incoming hook; omit if not hook-based.

deleted.description: True when the scenario has been soft-deleted (moved to the recycle bin). Defaults to false in the response when the row is active. Clients can filter on `deleted==true` to list bin contents.

deletedBy.description: ID of the user who moved this scenario to the recycle bin. Null for active scenarios and for deleted scenarios predating the audit column or created by system-driven deletes.

Unique numeric identifier for the hook.

name.description: Display name of the hook, assigned when the hook is created.

teamId.description: ID of the team this hook belongs to.

udid.description: Globally unique string identifier for the hook. This value forms the last path segment of the hook URL.

theme.description: Hex color code used to visually identify the hook in the Fusion scenario builder.

editable.description: Indicates whether the hook configuration can be edited.

queueCount.description: Number of incoming events currently queued for processing.

queueLimit.description: Maximum number of events the queue can hold before new incoming events are rejected.

enabled.description: Indicates whether the hook is active and accepting incoming events.

gone.description: When true, the hook returns a 410 Gone response. This happens when the hook is no longer attached to an active scenario.

learning.description: Indicates whether the hook is currently in learning mode, where it captures payloads to infer its data structure.

typeName.description: Type name that identifies the hook's integration. Workfront hooks begin with 'workfront-workfront' or 'workfront-maestro'.

data.description: Hook-specific configuration object. For Workfront hooks, this contains event subscription data. The shape varies by hook type.

scenarioId.description: ID of the scenario this hook is bound to. Returns null when the hook is not bound to a scenario.

url.description: The public URL that external systems use to send events to this hook. The last path segment is the hook UDID.

priority.description: Processing priority for the hook. Determines relative execution order when multiple hooks are queued. Possible values: Low, Medium, High.

detached.description: Indicates whether the hook has been detached, meaning it no longer has an active subscription in the external system.

connectionId.description: ID of the connection associated with this hook. Present when the hook was created using a connection.

automation.description: Owner binding for this hook, projected from users.company_device.automation. Agent shape: {type:'agent', id, triggerId, versionId}. Scenario shape: {type:'scenario', id}. Null when the hook is not bound. The wire shape never includes the legacy automation.agentId — consumers always read automation.id.

id.description: Unique numeric identifier of the data store

teamId.description: ID of the team that owns this data store. Filterable: pass property=teamId=<id> to scope the list to a single team; omit for an org-wide list.

records.description: Count of records stored in the data store

size.description: Current storage used by the data store, in bytes (e.g. 2097152 = 2 MiB)

maxSize.description: Maximum allowed storage capacity, in bytes (set via create/patch maxSizeMB × 1,048,576; e.g. 10485760 = 10 MiB)

id.description: Unique identifier for the execution. A 32-character lowercase string.

type.description: How the execution was run. `auto` = scheduled/automatic run, `manual` = user-initiated run-once.

kind.description: Type of entity this execution belongs to. `scenario` = automation scenario, `dlq` = incomplete execution.

kindId.description: Identifier of the parent entity referenced by `kind` (the scenario or DLQ id). Numeric id represented as a string.

teamId.description: Identifier of the team that owns the parent automation.

organizationId.description: Identifier of the organization that owns the execution.

authorId.description: Identifier of the user who authored/initiated the execution. Absent for fully automated runs with no acting user.

status.description: Execution result status code: `0` running, `1` success, `2` warning, `3` error.

trigger.description: Trigger type that initiated this execution: `webhook` (incoming HTTP trigger), `chat` (agent chat), `a2a` (agent-to-agent), `mcp` (MCP tool call), `scheduled` (time-based).

timestamp.description: Execution start time, as an ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC.

duration.description: Total execution wall-clock time, in milliseconds.

verifier.description: True for manual runs, which are run to verify/test the automation; false for automatic runs.

bundles.description: Total number of data bundles processed across all modules during the execution.

operations.description: Total number of module operations performed during the execution.

transfer.description: Total amount of data transferred during the execution, in bytes.

modules.description: Per-module operation statistics. Each entry contains `package` (app/connector package), `module` (module name), and `operations` (operations performed by that module).

processing.description: True while the execution is still being processed; false once it has completed. Logs may be partial while this is true.

config.description: Scenario runtime configuration snapshot. Boolean flags: `dlq`, `instant`, `dataloss`, `listener`, `parallel`, `autoCommit`, `sequential`, `localAccess`, `confidential`. Numbers: `roundtrips`, `maxFileSize` (bytes), `timeout` (milliseconds).

Authorization.description:
**Required.** IMS access token for authenticating the user or technical account making the request.

See the [Authentication guide](https://developer-stage.adobe.com/workfront-fusion-apis/getting-started/authentication/) for detailed instructions on obtaining access tokens.

[API Headers Documentation](https://developer-stage.adobe.com/workfront-fusion-apis/getting-started/api_headers/)

Organization ID.name: x-organization-id
Organization ID.description:
**Required.** Your Fusion Organization ID. Must be a number. Scopes all requests to your specific Fusion organization. You can find this ID in the Fusion Org Overview page URL: `/organization/{organizationId}/dashboard`.

**Example:** `12345`

[API Headers Documentation](https://developer-stage.adobe.com/workfront-fusion-apis/getting-started/api_headers/)

API Key.name: x-api-key
API Key.description:
**Required.** Your application's Client ID from Adobe Developer Console. This identifies your application and is the same value used for IMS authentication.

[API Headers Documentation](https://developer-stage.adobe.com/workfront-fusion-apis/getting-started/api_headers/)

Region.name: x-gw-region
Region.description:
**Required.** Routes requests to the correct Fusion regional instance.

**Example:** `or2`

[API Headers Documentation](https://developer-stage.adobe.com/workfront-fusion-apis/getting-started/api_headers/)
